methods.name: Peer-Median

data.narrative:
Sage Geosystems, a Series B climate and energy company founded by Cindy Taff and Lance Cook, is evaluated against a universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Linamar, ticker LNZA). The target has raised $114M+ to date.

Two valuation methods anchor this analysis. The stage-progression approach applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-later-stage progression, using the $114M raised as a proxy base, yielding $217M. The peer-median method references three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C)—producing a median of $1.0B and a range of $700M to $3.0B. 

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $184M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $608M. The wide spread reflects the tension between stage-based fundamentals—which favor a tighter $217M estimate—and peer comparables, where later-stage peers command substantially higher valuations. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of applying Series C multiples to a Series B asset, and the degree to which Sage's specific technology and market position justify positioning within the peer range. The median estimate of $608M represents a reasonable midpoint given current data constraints.
